<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" id="diagram" width="600" height="100"
     viewBox="0 0 600 100" class="l1-ok l2-ok">
  <style>
    /* --- the quiet furniture ------------------------------------------------------------- */
    .card { fill: #ffffff; stroke: #c0bfbc; stroke-width: 2; }
    .seam { fill: none; stroke: #c0bfbc; stroke-width: 2; }
    .dim { fill: #deddda; }
    .spark { fill: #613583; }
    .badge { fill: #ffffff; stroke-width: 2; }
    #diagram.dark .card { fill: #383838; stroke: #5e5c64; }
    #diagram.dark .seam { stroke: #5e5c64; }
    #diagram.dark .dim { fill: #5e5c64; }
    #diagram.dark .spark { fill: #d9c2f0; }
    #diagram.dark .badge { fill: #303030; }

    .link { fill: none; stroke-width: 4; stroke-linecap: round; }
    .glyph { fill: none; stroke-width: 2.6; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }
    .glyph-fill { stroke: none; }

    /* --- the four link states ------------------------------------------------------------
       Each one draws its own line, badge ring and mark, so colour is never the only difference
       between two of them: a broken line and an X differ from a solid line and a tick with the
       screen in greyscale (ADR 0025 § 4). Adwaita green 5 / yellow 5 / red 3 / dark 2 on light,
       and the lighter rungs of the same columns on dark. */
    .st { display: none; }
    .ok .link, .ok .badge, .ok .glyph { stroke: #26a269; }
    .wait .link, .wait .badge { stroke: #e5a50a; }
    .wait .glyph-fill { fill: #e5a50a; }
    .fail .link, .fail .badge, .fail .glyph { stroke: #e01b24; }
    .unknown .link, .unknown .badge, .unknown .glyph { stroke: #77767b; }
    .unknown .glyph-fill { fill: #77767b; }
    #diagram.dark .ok .link, #diagram.dark .ok .badge, #diagram.dark .ok .glyph { stroke: #33d17a; }
    #diagram.dark .wait .link, #diagram.dark .wait .badge { stroke: #f6d32d; }
    #diagram.dark .wait .glyph-fill { fill: #f6d32d; }
    #diagram.dark .fail .link, #diagram.dark .fail .badge, #diagram.dark .fail .glyph { stroke: #f66151; }
    #diagram.dark .unknown .link, #diagram.dark .unknown .badge, #diagram.dark .unknown .glyph { stroke: #9a9996; }
    #diagram.dark .unknown .glyph-fill { fill: #9a9996; }

    #diagram.l1-ok      #link1 .ok      { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l1-wait    #link1 .wait    { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l1-fail    #link1 .fail    { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l1-unknown #link1 .unknown { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l2-ok      #link2 .ok      { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l2-wait    #link2 .wait    { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l2-fail    #link2 .fail    { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l2-unknown #link2 .unknown { display: inline; }

    /* "You are here", variant A: an outline in the app accent, never a fill — the own node is
       marked, not praised, so green keeps meaning "this link works" and nothing else. Variant B
       (the default) draws no ring at all and lets the host's accent pill under the name say it.
       The ring's footprint is reserved in the geometry either way, which is why switching the
       variant moves nothing: every link already ends a gap short of it (ADR 0025 § 2). */
    #ring-beifahrer, #ring-browser { fill: none; stroke: #613583; stroke-width: 3; display: none; }
    #diagram.dark #ring-beifahrer, #diagram.dark #ring-browser { stroke: #d9c2f0; }
    #diagram.mark-ring.here-window #ring-beifahrer { display: inline; }
    #diagram.mark-ring.here-extension #ring-browser { display: inline; }

    /* The pause is the person's own stop and no link state, so it sits ON the browser as a badge
       (ADR 0005). Only the extension ever sets it: the bridge is never told (ADR 0015 § 5). */
    #pause-dot { fill: #e5a50a; stroke: #ffffff; stroke-width: 3; }
    #pause-bars { fill: #241f31; }
    #diagram.dark #pause-dot { fill: #f6d32d; stroke: #383838; }

    /* Two counts, two stacks: agent sessions on the left (ADR 0007), connected browsers on the
       right. Both are the same drawing offset behind the front card, and neither changes the
       artwork's size — "+ n more" is a word the host writes, not a card. */
    #stack-2, #stack-3, #bstack-2, #bstack-3, #pause { display: none; }
    #diagram.stacked-2 #stack-2, #diagram.stacked-3 #stack-2 { display: inline; }
    #diagram.stacked-3 #stack-3 { display: inline; }
    #diagram.browsers-2 #bstack-2, #diagram.browsers-3 #bstack-2 { display: inline; }
    #diagram.browsers-3 #bstack-3 { display: inline; }

    /* One browser connected, another gone: the OUTERMOST card of the browser stack turns into a
       dashed empty outline. The host sets browsers-(connected + 1) together with browser-gone,
       so the count a person sees is the total and the ghost is always the rear one. Dashed and
       unfilled rather than a colour, so it tells apart in greyscale like every link state does
       (ADR 0025 § 4). The bridge has exactly one of these to report — BridgeStatus.disconnected
       is a single BrowserGone — which is why one ghost is enough and link 2 stays ok: an agent
       can still act in the browser that IS there. */
    #diagram.browser-gone #bstack-2 .card { fill: none; stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
    #diagram.browsers-3.browser-gone #bstack-2 .card { fill: #ffffff; stroke-dasharray: none; }
    #diagram.browsers-3.browser-gone #bstack-3 .card { fill: none; stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
    #diagram.dark.browsers-3.browser-gone #bstack-2 .card { fill: #383838; }

    #diagram.paused #pause { display: inline; }
  </style>

    .ok .link, .ok .badge, .ok .glyph { stroke: #26a269; }
    .wait .link, .wait .badge { stroke: #e5a50a; }
    .wait .glyph-fill { fill: #e5a50a; }
    .fail .link, .fail .badge, .fail .glyph { stroke: #e01b24; }
    .unknown .link, .unknown .badge, .unknown .glyph { stroke: #77767b; }
    .unknown .glyph-fill { fill: #77767b; }
    #diagram.dark .ok .link, #diagram.dark .ok .badge, #diagram.dark .ok .glyph { stroke: #33d17a; }
    #diagram.dark .wait .link, #diagram.dark .wait .badge { stroke: #f6d32d; }
    #diagram.dark .wait .glyph-fill { fill: #f6d32d; }
    #diagram.dark .fail .link, #diagram.dark .fail .badge, #diagram.dark .fail .glyph { stroke: #f66151; }
    #diagram.dark .unknown .link, #diagram.dark .unknown .badge, #diagram.dark .unknown .glyph { stroke: #9a9996; }
    #diagram.dark .unknown .glyph-fill { fill: #9a9996; }

    #diagram.l1-ok      #link1 .ok      { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l1-wait    #link1 .wait    { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l1-fail    #link1 .fail    { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l1-unknown #link1 .unknown { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l2-ok      #link2 .ok      { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l2-wait    #link2 .wait    { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l2-fail    #link2 .fail    { display: inline; }
    #diagram.l2-unknown #link2 .unknown { display: inline; }

    /* "You are here", variant A: an outline in the app accent, never a fill — the own node is
       marked, not praised, so green keeps meaning "this link works" and nothing else. Variant B
       (the default) draws no ring at all and lets the host's accent pill under the name say it.
       The ring's footprint is reserved in the geometry either way, which is why switching the
       variant moves nothing: every link already ends a gap short of it (ADR 0025 § 2). */
    #ring-beifahrer, #ring-browser { fill: none; stroke: #613583; stroke-width: 3; display: none; }
    #diagram.dark #ring-beifahrer, #diagram.dark #ring-browser { stroke: #d9c2f0; }
    #diagram.mark-ring.here-window #ring-beifahrer { display: inline; }
    #diagram.mark-ring.here-extension #ring-browser { display: inline; }

    /* The pause is the person's own stop and no link state, so it sits ON the browser as a badge
       (ADR 0005). Only the extension ever sets it: the bridge is never told (ADR 0015 § 5). */
    #pause-dot { fill: #e5a50a; stroke: #ffffff; stroke-width: 3; }
    #pause-bars { fill: #241f31; }
    #diagram.dark #pause-dot { fill: #f6d32d; stroke: #383838; }

    /* Two counts, two stacks: agent sessions on the left (ADR 0007), connected browsers on the
       right. Both are the same drawing offset behind the front card, and neither changes the
       artwork's size — "+ n more" is a word the host writes, not a card. */
    #stack-2, #stack-3, #bstack-2, #bstack-3, #pause { display: none; }
    #diagram.stacked-2 #stack-2, #diagram.stacked-3 #stack-2 { display: inline; }
    #diagram.stacked-3 #stack-3 { display: inline; }
    #diagram.browsers-2 #bstack-2, #diagram.browsers-3 #bstack-2 { display: inline; }
    #diagram.browsers-3 #bstack-3 { display: inline; }

    /* One browser connected, another gone: the OUTERMOST card of the browser stack turns into a
       dashed empty outline. The host sets browsers-(connected + 1) together with browser-gone,
       so the count a person sees is the total and the ghost is always the rear one. Dashed and
       unfilled rather than a colour, so it tells apart in greyscale like every link state does
       (ADR 0025 § 4). The bridge has exactly one of these to report — BridgeStatus.disconnected
       is a single BrowserGone — which is why one ghost is enough and link 2 stays ok: an agent
       can still act in the browser that IS there. */
    #diagram.browser-gone #bstack-2 .card { fill: none; stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
    #diagram.browsers-3.browser-gone #bstack-2 .card { fill: #ffffff; stroke-dasharray: none; }
    #diagram.browsers-3.browser-gone #bstack-3 .card { fill: none; stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
    #diagram.dark.browsers-3.browser-gone #bstack-2 .card { fill: #383838; }

    #diagram.paused #pause { display: inline; }
  </style>
